What's new

Version 173 · A brand new look, cruise button, real Tesla visualization

⚡ Way less lag

  • Distant cars are now drawn together in one go instead of one by one. The city went from about 1,970 draw calls per frame to about 830, so frames are much smoother, especially on phones.
  • Car physics run about 4× faster: crash checks no longer loop over every parked car in the world each step.
  • AI traffic only checks for cars near it instead of all 2,000+ parked cars.
  • Far-away traffic uses simple wheels, and your tire tread only renders when you can actually see it. On Low and Lowest, small details like signs and bumps stop drawing sooner.

📱 CarPlay and Android Auto redone

  • CarPlay now looks like iOS 26: a glass sidebar with your recent apps, the blue wave wallpaper, a 5×2 app grid with page dots, and a dashboard with the map plus glass cards for your next turn, Now Playing and your day.
  • Android Auto now looks like the 2026 redesign: the map fills the screen, a floating rail on the left (apps, Gemini ✦, app grid), a green turn card, an ETA chip, floating message and album-art media cards, and the clock widget on wide screens. The app grid opens over a wallpaper with the map still showing on the side.

📻 More radio

  • The live radio now loads up to 60 stations, including ones that stream in HLS format (a lot of the big FM stations, like 97.1 The Ticket, use it). Detroit stations show their real spot on the dial (97.1, 101.1, 95.5, 760 AM and more).

🎨 Screen themes

  • Settings › Cluster › Screen theme: Ocean Blue, Racing Red, Emerald, Gold, Violet or Midnight, for every brand's screens. The Themes button on the Cadillac home works now too.

🔧 Fixes

  • Parallel park assist works with big trucks now. The F-150 and Ram used to back into the car behind and get stuck on "Straightening". The parking sensors were measuring from a normal-size car's bumper, so long cars got wrong distances too. Fixed for every car.
  • Buying a phone on mobile: the store is a compact grid that fits the screen and works with a tap. After you buy, it goes straight to the home screen.
  • The Settings app no longer lets you switch phones for free. Use "Get a new phone" to sell yours back for half price.
  • On short (landscape) phone screens, the home screen hides the big widgets so the app icons aren't cut in half.

📱 Phones

  • You start without a phone now. Open the phone and the store pops up: iPhone 17 ($799), iPhone 17 Pro ($1,099), iPhone Duo ($1,999), moto g ($199), Pixel 10 ($799), Galaxy S26 Ultra ($1,299) and Galaxy Z Fold 8 ($1,899). No phone = no CarPlay/Android Auto.
  • The iPhone Duo and Z Fold 8 fold: tap the fold button to open the big inner screen with more apps per row.
  • The Lottery app is on the home screen now (it was hidden), and it has a proper header.
  • Fixed icons and tabs overlapping on the phone: the home screen scrolls and app tabs scroll sideways instead of squishing.

🅿️ Realistic parking sensors

  • New sensor display: a top view of your car with green, yellow and red bars around it for each sensor, plus side bars on cars with side sensors. Shows the distance and STOP when you're close. Audis use their white and red style.

🔧 Fixes

  • Fixed the red "reading 's.L'" error that could freeze the game or the camera view (Volvo EX30 and others).
  • Less lag: physics can't pile up after a slow frame anymore, and the sensors stop scanning for objects above about 15 mph.

🎟️ Lottery

  • New Lottery app on your phone. Scratch-offs: Lucky 7s ($2, top prize $10,000), Cash Blast ($10, $250,000) and Millionaire ($30, $1,000,000). You find out right away.
  • Mega draw: $2 for 5 numbers plus a Mega ball, drawn every night at 11 PM. The jackpot starts at $5,000,000 and grows with every ticket. You get a message with the numbers either way.
  • The odds are like the real thing, so it's for fun, not a money glitch 😅

🔧 Fixes

  • The parking sensor display on the screen is smaller now, and the rear segments were on the wrong side (left showed on the right). Fixed.
  • Chevy EVs (Equinox EV, Blazer EV, Silverado EV, Bolt) get their blue EV cluster back.
  • Fixed the "reading 'toLowerCase'" error that could pop up when the browser autofilled something.

🎁 Codes and a fresh start

  • Everyone starts fresh: money, cars, garage, bank, loans, stocks and gigs were reset for every player, on your device and in your account. Your settings, character and achievements stay.
  • New: redeem codes. Settings › Spawn › 🎁 Redeem a code. Codes are for a limited time and each one works once.
  • Code 1MILL gives you $1,000,000. It works once, then never again on that device or account, and it stops working at 12 AM Eastern tonight.
  • Resetting your car now fixes flat, leaking and shredded tires too.
  • The parking sensor display now shows up on the center screen in every gear (Drive, Reverse, Neutral) whenever something is close, side zones included, not just in Neutral.
  • Tesla upgrades you buy (Full Self-Driving, FSD subscription, Acceleration Boost, Premium Connectivity) now save with that car and stay after you reload. They also cost real money now: $8,000 for FSD, $99 a month for the subscription, and so on.

🎛️ More real clusters

  • New Audi virtual cockpit on the 2025 Q5, Q6 e-tron, A6 allroad and Q3: black, slim white dials with red sweeps, your car on the road between them (the lanes turn green with lane assist), red speed limit ring and drive select mode.
  • New Ford Digital Experience cluster on the 2026 Explorer and Expedition: big speed at the top, your car on the road, and tall fuel and temperature bars on the sides.
  • New Honda / Acura digital cluster on the Google built-in cars (Pilot, Passport, Prelude, Sport Touring hybrids, MDX, ADX): two blue (red on Acura) ringed dials and your car in the middle.
  • Full-screen navigation in the cluster: pick Navigation with J and Chevy, GMC, Buick, Ford, Jeep, Ram, Hyundai, Kia, Nissan, Toyota and more fill the whole cluster with the map, like the real GM and VW ones, with speed on top, the turn card, arrival time and gauges along the bottom.
  • On these clusters the J card sits in the middle where the real info screen is, and "Standard" brings back the road view.

🎛️ Cluster styles

  • Mercedes now has the real Display style setting (Settings › Cluster › Display style). Classic is the two blue dials. Sporty is red, with one big rev/power dial and digital speed in the middle, your trip card on the left and a G-force meter on the right. Discreet is black with just the speed, gear, speed limit and range.
  • The 2019 Audi Q5 virtual cockpit gets the real view button (Settings › Cluster › Virtual cockpit view). Classic gives you the big dials, and Infotainment puts the map in the middle.

🐛 Bug fixes

  • Fixed the game freezing with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'L')". An AI car could lose its path halfway through a roundabout or junction and stop the whole game, which also made your car stop steering (the Lucid Air Sapphire report). Now that car just carries on along the road.
  • Fixed the "reading 'how'" error after driving one of your own cars from My Garage.
  • Fixed the camera page on BMW, Mercedes, Audi, Genesis, Lucid, Rivian and Honda/Acura screens. It wasn't picking the right views, so you now get the top view next to the rear or front camera like the real cars.

🚙 2026 RAV4 cluster

  • The 2026 RAV4 gets the new Toyota cluster from the photo: a thin ring around the speed that fills with power (green when it regenerates), EV / READY, P R N D, the speed limit sign, your car and the lanes on the right (green when Lane Tracing is on), and the cluster card on the left. Press J to switch it between Trip, Hybrid System, Driver Assist, Navigation, Tires and Media.

🚗 Your cars spawn right away · 🗺️ maps in the cluster

  • In My Garage, "Drive it" now just puts you in your car. No more landing on the builder's Finance page, no test-drive timer, and no "Where do you want to go?" pop-up. It shows up right where you were (or at your start point).
  • New Navigation view for the cluster on every car (J or Settings › Cluster › Cluster screen): a live map with your route and the next turn, like the map in real Audi, VW, GM, Jeep and Volvo clusters. On Lucid it fills the left panel, on Mercedes the middle box, and on other cars it opens a wide map in the middle of the cluster.

🖥️ Ford, Chevy/GMC/Buick and Subaru home screens

  • 2026 Explorer and the Expedition get Ford Digital Experience: a big map card with "Where to?" and the turn card, plus your profile card and a media card with play controls.
  • Chevy, GMC and Buick with Google built-in get the real split home: a media card on the left and Google Maps on the right with Search, Set Home and Set Work, and an "All apps" button for the full app grid.
  • 2026 Outback, Trailseeker and Uncharted get the new Subaru screen: a blue lake-and-mountains wallpaper, big clock and date, the radio pill up top, and the FM Radio and Recent Calls cards.

🅿️ Side parking sensors and smarter AEB

  • Cars with automatic parking now use their side sensors too, like Audi's park assist with 360° display. Three zones down each side warn you about walls, pillars, posts and cars beside you, and a steady tone sounds if you're about to scrape one.
  • Parking sensors now pick up walls, pillars and posts, not just cars, so the garage beeps for real.
  • Audis get the real parking system plus display on the screen: your car from above with white, orange and red segments front, rear and along the sides, and STOP when you're close.
  • Traffic cones no longer set off automatic emergency braking or the collision warning (front or rear). The parking sensors still beep for them.

📻 New radio page on most cars

  • The Media page on Toyota, Lexus, Hyundai, Kia, Nissan, Subaru, Mazda, VW, Ford, GM, Jeep, Ram and more is redone like the real bZ4X screen: sources on the left (Favorites, Tune, FM, AM, SiriusXM, Bluetooth), your live stations as tiles with their dial numbers, and a now-playing bar with skip and pause. No more overlapping buttons.
  • The Ram home screen's map no longer has buttons piled on top of the Search bar.

🌈 Ambient Lighting, McIntosh and Performance Pages

  • New Ambient Lighting page for every car that has it (Settings › Seats & Comfort › Ambient Lighting): six colour swatches, a brightness slider, and the cabin from above glowing in your colour. It changes the real lights in the car.
  • Jeeps with McIntosh audio get the blue McIntosh VU meters, and the needles move with the music. Open it from the McIntosh tile on the Jeep home screen or Settings › Sound.
  • Ram, Jeep, Dodge and Chrysler get Performance Pages (Settings › Drive Mode, or the Perf Pages tile on Jeeps): a G-force meter with a trail and peak, gauges for engine, power, speed and fuel, and a 0–60 timer.

🔴 Audi and 🟤 Genesis screens

  • New Audi MMI on the 2025 Q5, Q6 e-tron, A6 allroad and Q3: black screen with white type and red highlights, your car from above with live energy flow lines, tiles for Navigation, Media, Phone and Audi drive select (tap it to change modes), and the real bottom bar with temperatures.
  • 2019 Q5 gets MMI navigation plus: the car picture with the main menu (Navigation, Radio, Media, Telephone, Car, Camera).
  • Genesis gets the new wide-screen home with the date and a row of tall picture tiles (Navigation, Media, Vehicle, Climate, Energy, Phone), a new bottom bar, and the white-face dials from the GV70, with your car on the road in the middle.

🚙 2026 RAV4 home screen

  • The 2026 RAV4 gets the new Toyota home screen from the real car: three big cards for Media (with play controls), your RAV4 in its real paint (fuel, range and a Lock button) and Weather.

🔋 Hybrid monitor and cluster screens on every car

  • Every car's cluster can now show a card in the middle: Trip, Energy (EVs), Hybrid System (hybrids, with live arrows from the engine and battery to the wheels), Fuel Economy, Driver Assist, Tire Pressure or Media. Press J or use Settings › Cluster › Cluster screen. "Standard" puts the cluster back the way it was.

🅷 Honda and Acura with Google built-in

  • The cars that really have Google built-in get its screen: 2026 Pilot, 2027 Passport, 2027 Prelude, the Civic and CR-V Sport Touring Hybrids, Civic Si, MDX and ADX A-Spec.
  • Left rail like the real car (Home, Back, Google Assistant, Maps, FM, Smartphone Projection, Camera, Settings), app tiles (Maps, Phone, FM, Play Store, Smartphone Projection, Power Flow, Alexa, Google Assistant), and the right-hand panel with your name and the time.
  • Tap the right-hand panel to flip through widgets: Honda Power Flow on hybrids (the car from above with the engine, battery bars and moving arrows), Compass on Acuras, Now Playing and Trip. Power Flow also opens full screen from its tile.

🇸🇪 Volvo screens updated

  • Volvo center screens now come in dark mode like the real Google built-in cars (EX30, EX40, EX90, XC40, XC60, XC90). Switch back to light in Settings › Cluster › Display theme.
  • New Applications page like the real one: round Google-style icons (Bluetooth Media Player, Radio, Phone, Google Assistant, Google Maps, SiriusXM, Messages, Android Auto, Apple CarPlay, Settings, Camera, Driving Journal…) plus User manual and Get more apps.
  • The XC40, XC60 and XC90 cluster shows a Trip / Energy / Tires / Media card in the middle (J switches it). The time at the top of the screen no longer gets cut off.
  • Settings › Cluster now has a "Cluster screen" button on every car, so phone players can switch cluster views too.

⭐ Real Mercedes MBUX

  • Every Mercedes and Maybach gets the new MBUX home: the map fills the screen with a "Where to?" bar, a card of your car in its real paint, and media and phone cards you can tap.
  • Real climate bar along the bottom: big temperature boxes with AUTO on both ends, Back / Home / Apps / Vehicle in the middle, seat heat, fan, Climate menu and defrost.
  • New Apps page with the tilted MBUX icons: Navigation, Media, Phone, Comfort, Settings, Vehicle, Camera, Charging, Climate and Parking.
  • Cluster redone like the real Classic layout: speed and limit sign at the top, a "From Start" trip box in the middle (J switches it to Energy, Driver Assist, Tires or Media), time, range, and P R N D under the right dial.

🔵 Real BMW screens

  • Every BMW gets the new BMW Operating System 9 look: Suggestions (Weather, Parking, Drive Recorder), a media widget, navigation and vehicle status cards, and your My Modes along the bottom (Personal, Sport, Efficient and more).
  • New BMW bottom bar: temperature and seat heat on both ends, then Media, Phone, Home, Apps, Vehicle and Climate. The Apps button opens a full app grid.
  • The 2027 iX3 gets Panoramic iDrive: the band along the bottom of the windshield with speed limit and range, speed and gear, lane assist, navigation, battery and the BMW roundel, plus green head-up guidance above it. The last box shows the cluster view you pick with J. The iX3 center screen splits into widgets on the left and the map on the right.

🛠️ Better controls screen

  • The Driver Assistance page that most cars use has been redone: no more cut-off labels or crossing lines. Your car from above sits in the middle, with clean tiles on both sides that show how many features in each group are on (like "2 of 2 on").

🤎 Real Lucid Glass Cockpit and Pilot Panel

  • Lucid Air and Gravity get the real Glass Cockpit: a speed ring in the middle with P R N D, the car's "Air" or "Gravity" script with your range, and the Lucid home on the right (time, Home and Work shortcuts, now playing).
  • The left side of the cluster now switches between Trip, Energy, Driver Assist, Tire Pressure and Media. Press J (Shift+J goes back), or pick it in Settings.
  • New Pilot Panel (the lower screen) like the real car: a bottom menu with climate on both ends and Climate, Vehicle, Media, Settings, Seats and Park.
  • Vehicle page: your car from above in its real paint, Open Frunk / Open Trunk, lock, drive mode (Smooth, Swift, Sprint, Terrain) and lights, plus range, battery, odometer and tires.
  • Pull down from the top of the screen for Quick Controls: wipers, defrost, lock, frunk, trunk, fold mirrors and auto hold.
  • A new controls screen: Driver Assistance, Drive (modes, regen, auto hold), Display, Lights, Charging limit and Trip Info, all with switches that work. Seats page with heat, vent and massage.

⚫ New dark Tesla screen

  • Tesla screens now use the new dark look from the 2025 Model Y: dark driving visualization with your battery % next to P R N D, and the cruise set speed (MAX) under the speed limit sign.
  • New bottom bar like the real car: car icon, ‹ 70 › climate, then colored app tiles (Nav, Media, Camera, Energy, Autopilot, Toybox, Upgrades) and volume.
  • New Media app on Teslas with the live radio stations.
  • Controls › Display › Appearance now really works: Auto, Dark or Light.

🖥️ Real Rivian screen

  • Rivian R1S and R1T get the real Rivian center screen: black status bar on top (lock, profile, garage, alerts), and the real bottom dock with climate on both ends, seat heat, defrost, and Nav, Media, Vehicle, Camera, Energy and Settings.
  • Vehicle page like the real truck: On-Road / Off-Road drive mode tiles, ride height, Ride Feel, regen and stability, plus Compass, Elevation, Trip, Battery, Tires and Motor temp widgets that use your real numbers.
  • Media page with the live radio stations, and a Settings page with light/dark/auto theme, units, Highway Assist, lane keep, blind spot and walk-away lock.

📻 Radio fixes

  • The made-up game stations are gone: the radio is only real live stations now.
  • Every radio button on every car's screen works with the live stations: seek, track, tune, presets (they show the real station numbers), play/pause and the station lists.
  • The radio no longer switches itself on when you start the game or the car: press play. It turns off when you switch the car off or walk away from it.

📡 Real live radio

  • The car radio now plays real live stations, Detroit by default: SEEK and the presets go through the Detroit stations with their real dial numbers (101.9, 107.5, 760 AM…), real DJs and real ads.
  • Settings › Sound › Radio stations: pick Detroit, or real stations from across the US by genre (Hip-hop, Pop, Country, Rock, News & talk).
  • If a station is off the air the radio skips to the next one.

💡 Real blinkers, fog lights and welcome lights on every car

  • Blinkers now flash on the car's real headlights and taillights instead of small orange blocks in the corners. Each of the 270+ models works like the US car: an amber corner in the headlight, a daytime running light that turns amber (Ford, GM, Hyundai/Kia, Tesla and more), or a sequential sweep (Audi, Genesis, Lexus, Cadillac, Lincoln, Mach-E and more). Out back they're amber, or red sharing the tail lamp, or sequential.
  • Blinkers on the door mirrors on the cars that have them, and front fog lights in the bumper on the cars that have them (they light up with the fog light switch).
  • Welcome and goodbye lights: on cars that do it (Audi, Genesis, Lexus, Cadillac, Lincoln, Mercedes, BMW, Lucid, Rivian and more), the lamps sweep on when you unlock or start the car and sweep off when you lock it.
  • AI traffic blinks the same way.
  • Lane lines and your own mini car (in your paint, with its lights and blinkers) now show on every cluster that draws your lane, for cars with lane keeping, and the line you drift over flashes yellow.

🌲 Trees off means off, and straighter RAV4 lane lines

  • Turning Trees off (Settings › Graphics › custom, or the Low and Lowest presets) now removes every tree on the map, including the ones you could crash into: no more invisible trees to hit.
  • The mini car on the screens redraws less often on Low and Lowest graphics, which helps slow laptops like the Surface Go.
  • 2019 RAV4: the lane lines on the middle screen are straight again, angled like the real car, with your car between them, and the line that flashes is the one you are actually crossing.

🚫 No parking zones

  • The parking garage entrance and exit are clear again: no more parked cars or parking meters in front of the gates.
  • No parking in front of parking lots and drive-thru entrances, plus red-kerb stretches with NO PARKING signs around town. Park on a red kerb and you get a warning, then a $50 ticket after a minute.

🎨 Graphics settings, RAV4 gauges and a mini car on your screens

  • New Ultra graphics and a full custom graphics section (Settings › Graphics): resolution, view distance, traffic detail, trees, car shadows, mirror/screen refresh, anti-aliasing (MSAA or FXAA), ambient occlusion, bloom, light rays, depth of field, motion blur (and whether your own car blurs) and Simple/Full lighting. Picking a preset resets the custom rows.
  • Your own car on the screens: the Tesla visualization and the assist view now show a real mini model of your car in your paint, with headlights, brake lights and blinkers lighting up. On a Tesla, shift to Park and the car swings round to a studio view with Open Frunk / Open Trunk, the lock and the charge port.
  • 2019 RAV4 gauges redone from real photos: LE/XLE get two real dials (tachometer, or the hybrid CHG/ECO/PWR meter) with the small screen in the middle; Limited, Adventure and XSE Hybrid get the 7-in. screen on the left and a real speedometer. The middle screen shows the lane lines with your car between them (only on trims with lane assist), and the line you cross flashes yellow. Startup does the warning-light bulb check like the real car.
  • 2019 RAV4: cleaner blinker clicks from the real recording, and the hybrid only makes its AVAS hum in reverse (no cabin beep).
  • Full Self-Driving no longer creeps into a car that's right on its nose in a long queue.
  • Infotainment screens on every brand (except Tesla) now have a Home button.

🚙 New: 2025 Audi Q5 and SQ5

  • The all-new 2025 Audi Q5 (new model) in every US trim: Q5 Premium, Premium Plus and Prestige (2.0 TFSI, 268 hp, 295 lb-ft, 7-speed S tronic, quattro, 0-60 in about 5.8 s) and SQ5 Premium, Premium Plus and Prestige (3.0 TFSI V6 mild hybrid, 362 hp, 406 lb-ft, 0-60 in about 4.4 s).
  • Audi drive select with all six modes (comfort, balanced, dynamic, efficiency, offroad, individual). The SQ5 gets S sport suspension with damper control as standard; adaptive air suspension is an option on the Q5 Prestige and the SQ5.
  • Real features and packages: adaptive cruise assist with lane guidance, top view camera, head-up display, Bang & Olufsen 3D sound, Digital Matrix LED headlights, digital OLED taillights, park assist plus and the 10.9-in. passenger screen, by trim or as options. The 2019 Q5 is still there too.

🔇 Electric motor sound

  • On EVs and hybrids the electric motor hum now fades out together with the pedestrian warning sound (gone by about 19 mph), instead of whining the whole drive. It still plays in reverse.

🏠 Real infotainment home screens

  • The home screen on the center touchscreen now looks like each brand's real one, laid out from the owner's manuals and reviews: Kia, Hyundai and Genesis (map and media widgets with the weather, a row of menu icons underneath, Genesis in black and copper), Ford SYNC 4 (map on the left, swipeable Audio / Phone / weather / clock cards on the right with arrows), Chevrolet, GMC, Buick and Nissan (Google built-in: profile, pages of app icons, Google Assistant), Acura (map with tiles down the right side), Subaru STARLINK (starry background with colorful tiles), INFINITI InTouch (map on top, audio, climate, phone, apps, info and settings below), Chrysler Uconnect 5 (map, media and app cards), and Rivian (no home screen, like the real one: the map with a media column and the lock button top left).
  • 2019 RAV4: the Entune 3.0 home screen like the real 2019 RAV4 Hybrid: Audio top left with the four "Select & Hold to Add a Contact" buttons under it, and the Energy Monitor on the right (wheel, engine and battery joined by paths that light up red-orange from the engine, green from the battery and when braking charges it, with the battery cells showing the charge). The status icons sit next to the clock. The gas RAV4 shows the map (with navigation) or the clock there.

🚙 2019 RAV4 trims fixed

  • Added the gas LE, XLE Premium and Limited. Every trim now has only what the real one had: the LE (gas and hybrid) has no Blind Spot Monitor, Multi-Terrain Select is only on the Adventure and Limited, Intelligent Clearance Sonar with Rear Cross-Traffic Braking only comes with the Advanced Technology Packages, and the Limited's Bird's Eye View camera is in its package instead of standard. The XSE and Limited get the digital rearview mirror and blue ambient lighting, the Limited gets navigation, and the XLE Premium has its own Weather Package.

🔊 Real 2019 RAV4 and Toyota sounds

  • 2019 RAV4: recorded from a real one. The startup chime when it turns on, the turn-signal click, the seatbelt reminder (slow at first, faster after 20 seconds), the real reverse sound the car plays outside while backing up.
  • Every Toyota and Lexus: the real forward collision / emergency braking warning beep.

🚦 Leading vehicle departure on the cluster

  • When you're stopped behind a car and it pulls away while you don't, the cluster now pops up a "Leading vehicle is driving away" card (like Hyundai, Kia and Genesis show it): your car in the lane with the car ahead moving off up the road, together with the chime. It shows on the car's own cluster screen and pops up above the cluster in the new HUD, and goes away after a few seconds or as soon as you drive off. Works on every car with forward collision warning; you can still turn it off in Settings (next to Driver Attention Warning).

🚲 Smarter cyclists, heavier traffic, safer FSD

  • Genesis screens fixed: on the G80, GV60, GV70, Electrified GV70, GV80 and GV80 Coupe the gauges and the touchscreen were drawn on top of each other in the middle of the dash. The gauges now sit behind the steering wheel and the touchscreen to the right of them, like the real cars.
  • Update alerts are back: when a new update goes live while you're playing, the "A new version is out" bar shows up again with a Reload button (it only appeared for big version changes before), and this What's new screen shows the latest changes when you load in.
  • Cyclists stop getting stuck. When a parked car, a crashed car or a stopped bike is in the way at the kerb, they check over their shoulder, wait for a gap in traffic, swing out into the lane, pass it and tuck back in. Any that still get stuck out of sight are swapped for a new rider.
  • Traffic has real weight. Every AI car now weighs what that model really weighs (a Civic about 3,100 lb, an F-150 about 5,500 lb, a Super Duty over 7,000 lb). Hitting a big truck in a small car barely moves it and stops you hard, a heavy SUV shoves a small car much further, and parked cars (in Park with the brake on) resist more and slide less.
  • FSD watches people properly. It now works out where each person crossing the road will be by the time the car gets there, so it slows down or stops for people stepping out, jaywalking or walking across a crosswalk, instead of only reacting once they're right in its path. People at crosswalks also wait if your car is already turning through the junction.
  • Non-Tesla cars are back to the classic Assist screen and sensor panel (lane lines, Lane Keeping Assist, cruise gap, blind spot), now with a 3D model of your own car in its real paint instead of the flat outline. Teslas keep the full FSD visualization.

🛻 New: 2022 Ford F-150, and every trim for the new cars

  • 2022 Ford F-150 SuperCrew (new model) in every trim: XL (3.3 V6), STX and XLT (2.7 EcoBoost), Lariat (5.0 V8), King Ranch and Platinum (3.5 EcoBoost), Limited (PowerBoost hybrid with BlueCruise), Tremor (FOX off-road shocks, e-locker, Rock Crawl) and Raptor (450 hp, Fox Live Valve dampers, coil-sprung rear, Baja mode). Each has its real drive modes (Normal, Eco, Sport, Tow/Haul, Slippery, Deep Snow/Sand, Mud/Rut), suspension, packages, wheels and interiors.
  • PowerBoost hybrid like the real truck: XLT, Lariat, King Ranch and Platinum PowerBoost added next to the Limited. 430 hp and 570 lb-ft from the 3.5 L EcoBoost plus a 35 kW motor inside the 10-speed with a 1.5 kWh battery. It pulls away and drives on electricity alone up to about 20 mph at light throttle, the engine stops and starts by itself, braking charges the battery, and Pro Power Onboard is 2.4 kW (7.2 kW on the Limited or as an option). The 2025 F-150 PowerBoost drives the same way now.
  • Genesis: every US trim now, with real drive modes (Sport+ on Sport Prestige), suspension (road-preview adaptive dampers, air suspension on the G90), packages and features. G70 2.5T / 2.5T Prestige / 3.3T Sport Prestige; G80 2.5T / Advanced / Sport Prestige / 3.5T Sport Prestige; G90 3.5T and 3.5T e-SC; GV60 Standard / Advanced / Performance; GV70 2.5T / Select / Advanced / Sport Prestige / 3.5T Sport Prestige; Electrified GV70 Advanced / Prestige; GV80 2.5T / 2.5T Advanced / 3.5T Advanced / 3.5T Prestige; GV80 Coupe 3.5T and 3.5T e-SC. GV70 and GV80 get Terrain Mode (Snow, Mud, Sand).
  • Chevrolet Bolt LT and RS (Super Cruise available), Malibu LS / RS / LT / 2LT, and the final Nissan Altima SV / SR / SR AWD, all with real drive modes, suspension and packages.

🎨 A brand new look

  • The whole HUD was redone with rounded cards in graphite and champagne gold. Prefer it light? Switch to Ivory in Settings › Car › HUD colors.
  • New cluster: big speed with the speed limit sign, a speed bar, PRND, a power / regen bar, range, outside temperature and the time.
  • The cluster screen now has ‹ › arrows to flip between Energy, Assist, Trip and Car, with a slide animation and page dots.
  • Cruise control button next to the cluster: tap it to turn cruise on. A bar pops up on top of the cluster to set the following distance and the speed with − / + (5 mph a tap). Tap again to turn it off.
  • The EV mode button is now a circle above the cruise button (hybrids and plug-ins).
  • Drive mode and Terrain are two small pills side by side under the cluster; tap one and its choices slide out of it, and it folds back up after you pick.
  • Every HUD button now has a little press-and-pop animation when you tap it.
  • New loading screen: a gold gauge whose needle sweeps up as the game loads, light trails racing past behind it and a new tip every few seconds. Works on PC, phones and landscape.
  • The Energy screen now works on the F-150 PowerBoost: engine, battery and motor flow, battery % and "Electric" when you're driving on the battery.
  • Top right: your money with a level ring, and labelled tiles for Garage, Spawn, Tests, Dealer, Full screen and More.
  • Settings, the spawn picker, What's new and the loading screen match the new look.
  • Fixed an error that could pop up while the other cars load in the background.

🚘 A new cluster

  • The speedometer is now a digital instrument cluster: one dark screen with a segmented speedometer on the left (ticks and numbers, turning orange when you're over the limit, with the speed limit sign underneath), a power / charge gauge around the gear on the right (orange for power, green when you're regenerating), the car screen in the middle and a status line along the bottom with your drive mode, cruise speed, range, outside temperature and the time.
  • The middle screen has four tabs: Energy (a top view of your car with the engine, battery and motor drawn in and moving arrows showing where the power goes, plus horsepower and battery or fuel %), Assist (cruise, lane keep, the car ahead and blind spots; on a Tesla it's a mini FSD view), Trip (mpg or mi/kWh, miles, drive time and a bar per 15 seconds) and Car (tyre pressures and body damage). Tap it for the big panel.
  • Drive and terrain modes are a list beside the cluster on PC; tap one to switch. On phones, tap the mode or terrain button to open it.
  • More room to see the road: cruise control, lane keep and Autosteer only pop up above the cluster while they're on, and the right-hand buttons fold behind one ••• button (signals and hazards stay out). The whole HUD is smaller too.
  • A cleaner look for the rest of the HUD: flat dark panels, the top-left buttons in one bar, money / time / level as one card, and labelled Lock / Phone / Pair buttons.

🤖 Tesla

  • The FSD visualization was rebuilt to look like the real car: a camera above and behind you, shaded 3D cars with yours in white, real road surfaces with kerbs, white lane lines and double yellow centre lines, stop lines, glowing traffic lights, a HOLD icon, the auto-headlight icon and your set speed as "MAX" beside the speed limit.

⚙️ Other changes

  • Faster loading, and a new loading screen that shows up straight away instead of a blank page.
  • Imperial units everywhere: mph, miles, feet, inches, pounds, °F and psi, and engine / motor power in horsepower.
  • Ford sounds: a new startup chime, and the real Ford forward collision warning beeps instead of the generic beep.
  • Saved games start fresh with this version.

Version 172 · The new map, 11 new cars, smarter navigation

🔄 Updates since launch

  • Fixed the new map freezing and crashing a few seconds after it loads (especially on phones and tablets).
  • Roundabouts (not the little turning circles) now have two lanes: the outer lane for the first exit, the inner lane to go further round. Traffic and Full Self-Driving pick the right lane from where they're going.
  • Full Self-Driving without a destination now picks an exit at roundabouts (usually straight on) instead of circling, using the right lane for it. At all-way stops it no longer sits waiting behind a car that is itself waiting for it: after a couple of seconds it takes its turn.
  • The old Halden map is gone for good: the new map is the only world now (the ?world=1 link no longer opens it).
  • Fixed the Grand Wagoneer L (and Kia K5) freezing as soon as you spawned: the camera stuck and the car wouldn't drive. Their engine type had no engine sound, which stopped the game every frame. The Grand Wagoneer L now has its own twin-turbo straight-six sound.
  • If the game ever hits an error, a small red bar now says what went wrong. Screenshot it and send it in so it can be fixed.
  • Suspension setup (Settings › Controls, or ☰ › Settings): fit adjustable coilovers ($1,800) and tune ride height, front and rear springs, dampers, anti-roll bars and camber on a live diagram of your car, or pick a preset (Comfort, Sport, Track, Drift, Stance, Lifted). It shows the ride frequency, body roll, ground clearance and whether the car will understeer or oversteer, and the car really drives that way: stiffer bars roll less, more camber grips harder in corners, and slamming it scrapes over bumps. Tap See it on the car to look at the coilovers in the wheel wells (shown through the body) while you adjust them: the car rises and drops, the springs change colour and size, and the wheels lean in with camber.
  • Full Self-Driving follows the navigation off the freeway again: it used to drift back onto the freeway at the start of an exit ramp. Navigation no longer says "Rerouting" when you take the exit it asked for.

🗺️ A whole new world

  • Halden is replaced by a much bigger map: Westport downtown, the town of Fairhaven, little Millbrook on the lake, the Rosedale and Kestrel Estates neighborhoods, country roads and farms, and Mount Kestrel with a switchback road to the summit.
  • Two interstates: I-38 (east–west) and I-61 (north–south), joined by a full cloverleaf, with diamond interchanges, exit numbers, mile markers, green guide signs and orange median lights at night.
  • Roundabouts where several roads meet, cul-de-sacs in the neighborhoods, and bridges over the Clearwater River, including an old covered bridge, a rusty truss bridge and a stone bridge. Gravel fords and low crossings flood when it rains hard: deep water slows you down and can stall a gas engine.
  • The off-road park sits up on the mountain now, with a log bridge on the trail, and the proving ground is off County Rd 1.

🍔 Places to go

  • Working drive-thrus at McDonald's, Burger King, Wendy's, Taco Bell, Chick-fil-A and KFC: order and pay at the speaker, then pick up at the window.
  • Dealerships on Route 20 (Ford, Toyota, Chevrolet, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Tesla): pull into the lot to shop, test drive or trade in. The service centers do recalls, software updates and alignments.
  • Paid street parking in the towns: $1 per 15 minutes, 2 hours max, and a $35 ticket if the meter runs out.
  • Kestrel Estates is gated: the arms lift for residents (buy a house there) or with a $20 guest pass.
  • Farms all over the countryside: corn, wheat and hay fields, red barns, silos and hay bales.

🚦 Life on the roads

  • School buses in the morning and mid-afternoon. When one stops, its red lights flash and the stop arm swings out: passing it is a $250 ticket.
  • A lane closure on I-38 eastbound with cones and a flagger: 45 mph, fines doubled, and a speed camera ($300).
  • The Jefferson Ave drawbridge opens every 4 minutes: bells, gates, the bridge lifts and a boat goes through.
  • A freight train runs between Westport and Fairhaven, with crossing gates on every road and a viaduct over the river.
  • Car meet every night after 8 PM in the Fairhaven Blvd lot.

⛰️ Mount Kestrel

  • The Kestrel Hill Climb: a timer from the foot of the switchbacks to the summit, with your 5 best times saved.
  • The summit road ices over in rain and snow, and there's frost early in the morning. Mind the "Chains required" sign.

🚗 11 new cars

  • Genesis G70, G80, G90, GV60, GV70, Electrified GV70, GV80 and GV80 Coupe; Chevrolet Bolt and Malibu; and the 2027 Nissan Altima.

🧭 Smarter navigation

  • Roundabouts are one instruction now: "At the roundabout, take the second exit onto County Rd 3".
  • Freeway ramps say where they go ("Take the ramp onto I-38 East") and exits give their number ("Take exit 4 to Fairhaven Blvd").
  • Places off the road (restaurants, dealerships, the car meet lot) take you to the right street and tell you which side your destination is on.
  • Every drive-thru, dealership, the service center, the hill climb, the drawbridge and the car meet are in the destination list.

🎮 Steering wheels

  • Force feedback now works on Moza, Fanatec, Simagic, Cammus and other direct-drive bases (Chrome or Edge on a computer): Settings › Controls › Steering wheel › Connect force feedback.

🌾 Also

  • Gig jobs use the real places: food pickups are at the fast-food restaurants, and the tow truck takes cars to the Route 20 auto shop.

Version 171 · Regen braking, battery temperature, trip summary, smarter range

🔋 EVs and hybrids

  • Pressing the brake pedal now charges the battery: gentle braking is done by the motor, and the regular brakes only join in for harder stops (or when ABS steps in). The energy screen shows the battery charging as you slow down.
  • Battery temperature: in the cold, an EV's battery limits regenerative braking and power until it warms up with driving. Push it hard for a long time and a hot battery limits power to protect itself.
  • Hybrids start and stop their engine more smoothly: it doesn't restart a moment after shutting off unless you need it, and it takes over the load gently instead of all at once.
  • Smart Regen (Hyundai, Kia and Genesis EVs): lift off and the car slows itself for the car ahead using regen. You can switch it off in the settings.

🧾 Trip summary

  • Switch the car off after a drive and it tells you how it went: distance, time, mpg, how much was on electricity, and an eco score out of 100 (hard stops and starts and speeding cost points).

⛽ Range that learns

  • The range estimate now follows how you've been driving over the last several miles: drive hard and it drops, cruise gently and it climbs, like a real car.

🌡️ Engines heat up when you work them

  • Climbing a long steep hill at full power, or towing a heavy trailer, now heats the engine up; on a hot day it can overheat and cut power until it cools.

Version 170 · Cylinder deactivation, tired engines

🟢 Cylinder deactivation

  • Engines that really shut off cylinders now do it: cruise gently once the engine is warm and they drop to half their cylinders, sound quieter and a bit duller, and use about 13% less fuel. Press harder and they're all back instantly.
  • Under their real names: Dynamic Fuel Management (Chevrolet, GMC and Cadillac V8s, 8 → 4), Fuel Saver (Ram, Jeep and Dodge HEMI V8s, 8 → 4), Variable Cylinder Management (Honda and Acura V6s, 6 → 3), Mazda's 2.5 (4 → 2), Active Cylinder Technology (VW Jetta and Taos, 4 → 2) and Audi's cylinder on demand (V8s, 8 → 4). The status line shows when it's on.

🛠️ Tired engines

  • An engine that's way overdue for an oil change or has very high miles now shows it: a rough, hunting idle, a little less power, slightly worse fuel economy, and blue smoke out the back when you floor it. An oil change helps right away.
  • A cold start puffs a little smoke from the exhaust.

Version 169 · Flat tires

🛞 Flat tires you can see and feel

  • As a tire loses air you can watch it squash flat against the road and bulge out at the sides, and that corner of the car sits lower.
  • A flat tire grips less, drags, and pulls the car toward that side: let go of the wheel at highway speed and you'll drift across a lane in a few seconds.
  • Keep driving on a flat (about a mile) and the tire comes apart: you're on the rim, with sparks off the wheel, grinding, the steering wheel shaking and very little grip.
  • BMWs have run-flat tires: a flat one stays almost upright and barely pulls. Keep it under 50 mph and you can drive a long way to get it fixed.

How you get one

  • Potholes can still start a slow leak (watch the tire pressure warning count down), and now a deep pothole at highway speed can blow a tire out instantly. Police spike strips flatten all four.

Fixing it

  • Tire pressure screen: Patch and fill ($35) for a leak or a flat, or Fit the spare if one has come apart. Tread Center replaces a shredded tire; gas stations still have air.

Version 168 · Real tires, turbo lag, cold starts

🛞 Real tires

  • Your car's tires are now real 3D tires built to its exact wheel size, with actual tread you can see up close: grooves and sipes on all-season tires, two wide grooves on summer tires, dense sipes on winter tires and chunky blocks with shoulder lugs on off-road tires. Fit a different tire type at Tread Center and the tread changes.
  • Rounded shoulders, a sidewall that bulges a little like a real tire, and a raised rim protector ridge.

🌀 Turbos

  • Turbo engines now have real lag: the turbo has to spin up before boost arrives. Floor it from low revs and there's a pause before the shove; at high revs it responds almost instantly.
  • You can hear it: the whistle rises as the turbo spools and winds down after you lift, and lifting off at full boost gives a proper blow-off "pssh".

❄️ Cold starts

  • Gas engines now start cold: the revs flare up as it catches, then it idles fast while it warms up and settles down as the temperature gauge rises (a few minutes). A cold engine uses more fuel and has a little less power.
  • Every car you get into starts at the outside temperature.

Version 167 · Turn signals fixed, BMW Uneven Road Surface warning, headlight self-test

↩️ Turn signals

  • Your signal no longer switches itself off after a couple of seconds while you're stopped or driving straight. Like a real car, it only cancels when the steering wheel comes back after a turn.
  • New setting: Self-cancelling turn signals. Turn it off and the signal stays on until you switch it off yourself.

🚗 Traffic

  • Cars no longer slam on the brakes the moment you put your signal on. Drivers in the lane you want only react if you're moving and already ahead of them, and not all of them do: calm drivers usually ease off to let you in, aggressive ones rarely do. The ones that let you in lift off the gas instead of stopping.

〰️ BMW Uneven Road Surface warning

  • BMWs now warn you about potholes, speed bumps, sewer covers, dips and railway tracks coming up on your road, between 0.1 and 0.25 mi ahead (along your route when navigating). Like the real one it's visual only, with no chime. You can turn it off in the safety settings.

💡 Headlight self-test

  • When the headlights come on (starting the car at night, or switching them on), the self-levelling headlights run their self-test: the beam dips down, sweeps up past normal and settles back, and swivelling headlights look left and right.

Version 166 · New notifications, a 40% hill

🔔 Notifications

  • Messages now stack down the left side of the screen as dark bars, newest at the bottom, so several can show at once instead of replacing each other. Warnings (damage, overheating, flat tyres, crashes) get a warning triangle, everything else an exclamation mark. Each one slides in and fades out after a few seconds.
  • Up to 7 at a time on a computer, 4 on a phone so they don't cover the controls. They never block taps.
  • The "time for a break?" reminder no longer pops up.

⛰️ Proving ground

  • New 40% hill: 12 m tall (three times the 20% hill) with guard rails, right after the 30% ramp. Take a run-up, or try a hill start halfway up and Downhill Assist on the way down.

Version 165 · Self-levelling headlights are back

💡 Self-levelling headlights

  • Self-levelling headlights are back on every car (they had gone missing from almost all of them). The beam aims at the road about 35 m ahead: it drops over the top of a hill instead of lighting up the sky, lifts into dips, and stays level when the car is loaded or squats under hard acceleration.
  • Turn it off in Settings under Active levelling to see the difference: the beam then pitches with the car. Your choice is remembered when you switch cars.

Version 164 · Real traction and stability control buttons, evasive steering on more cars

🛞 Traction and stability control like the real cars

  • The traction control button (T, or Settings) now works the way each maker's button does, with its real name. In the real car the second stage is a long press; here you press again.
  • Toyota and Lexus: TRAC OFF, then TRAC OFF + VSC OFF (only when stopped). Ford and Lincoln: traction control off, then AdvanceTrac sport mode. Chevrolet, GMC, Buick, Cadillac: TCS off, then TCS and StabiliTrak off. Jeep, Ram, Dodge, Chrysler: ESC Partial Off, then ESC Full Off. Hyundai, Kia, Genesis: traction off, then ESC OFF. Mazda: TCS OFF, then DSC OFF. Subaru: traction off, then VDC OFF. BMW: DTC, then DSC OFF. Audi and VW: ASR off, then ESC Sport.
  • Single-stage buttons: Honda and Acura VSA OFF, Nissan VDC OFF and Mercedes ESP OFF only reduce stability control, they never fully turn it off. Volvo has ESC Sport. Tesla has Slip Start, which only lets the wheels slip a little.
  • With stability control fully off, the car can really slide and spin. In sport stages it lets the car slide further before it steps in. The 2007 Mustang has traction control but no stability control, like the real one.
  • Every car starts with everything back on, like restarting a real car.

↪️ Evasive steering

  • Evasive steering assist is now on every car that has it in real life, under its real name: Toyota and Lexus Emergency Steering Assist (newest safety systems), Ford and Lincoln Evasive Steering Assist (Co-Pilot360), BMW Evasion aid, Mercedes Evasive Steering Assist, Audi evasive steering assist and Volvo City Safety steering support.

Version 163 · Battery slider fix

Fixes

  • Hybrids: setting the battery to 1% with the Charge slider (Settings › Controls) made it jump back to 12%. The slider now sets the charge you can actually use, the same number the gauges show, so 1% stays 1% and drains down to 0%.

Version 162 · Hybrid battery gauges fixed

Fixes

  • Hybrids and plug-in hybrids: some screens showed the battery stuck at 12% or more even when it was empty. Those screens counted the hidden reserve the car never uses. Every battery gauge now shows only the charge you can use, so it goes all the way down to 0%: the centre screen's energy and power-flow pages, the battery bars and the EV range.

Version 161 · The tow truck takes your car to the shop

🛻 Towing after a crash

  • When you tap "Send help" after a crash (or don't answer the call), the tow truck that comes now really takes your car. It parks in front of you, winches your car up onto the flatbed, and drives the real roads to Tread Center with you riding on the back. You can watch from outside or from the driver's seat.
  • The trip goes through traffic and stops at lights like any other truck. Tap "⏩ Skip to the shop" to get there right away.
  • At the shop your car is dropped in the lot by the service door, still damaged, and the repair menu opens so you can pick and pay for the repairs you want.
  • If you drive away before the truck gets there, it leaves without your car.

Version 160 · Lead vehicle departure alert

🚗 Lead vehicle departure alert

  • Stopped in traffic or at a light behind another car? If that car drives off and you don't, your car chimes and tells you traffic ahead is moving.
  • Every car with forward collision warning has it, under its real name: Leading Vehicle Departure Alert on Hyundai, Kia and Genesis (with the Kia/Hyundai chime), Front Departure Alert on Toyota and Lexus, Lead Vehicle Start Alert on Subaru.
  • It stays quiet when you pull away yourself, and when adaptive cruise control is handling stop-and-go for you. Hyundai, Kia and Genesis can turn it off in the car's settings.

Version 159 · Front cross-traffic braking, BMW sounds, camera button fix

🛑 Front cross-traffic braking

  • Cars with front cross-traffic alert (Mazda CX-5/50/70/90, Lexus, BMW, Audi, Lucid, Sequoia, Tundra, Grand Highlander, Crown) now brake on their own when you pull out in front of a car coming from the side that you can't see past the pillars or parked cars. It works up to about 13 mph, when automatic braking is on.
  • It warns first, then stops the car and holds it for a moment while the other car goes by. Press the brake hard to take over.

🔊 BMW sounds

  • BMWs now play the real BMW gong when you start the car and for the seatbelt reminder.
  • BMW forward collision warning and automatic braking use the real BMW alert sound.

Fixes

  • On phones, the camera button (switch between outside and the driver's seat) did nothing. It works again.

Version 158 · Phone fix: getting out of the full-screen centre screen

Fixes

  • On phones and tablets, tapping Screen to lean into the centre screen hid every button, so there was no way back. A "← Back to the road" button now sits in the top-left corner while the screen is enlarged. On PC, M or Esc still works too.

Version 157 · Crash physics for traffic, better multiplayer sync, buy button fix

💥 Traffic and parked cars react like real cars

  • Hit another car hard and it gets shoved by the impact: it spins if you hit it off-centre, skids on its tyres (the driver stands on the brakes; a parked car only has its parking brake) and comes to a stop.
  • Gravity: a car knocked off a ramp or a bridge falls, and cars lean with the ground they end up on.
  • A car that's sent flying bounces off walls and can knock into other cars, which start moving too.
  • When it stops, it rejoins its lane if it can. If it ended up sideways or off the road, it stays there with its hazards on for a while.

🌐 Multiplayer

  • You now see other players' headlights and high beams, their front wheels turning, their car leaning and diving, reversing, and their horn (quieter the farther away they are).
  • Crashing into another player pushes their car too, on their screen.
  • Everyone on a server shares the same day as well as the same time and weather.

Fixes

  • Buying a car: the big button now says what it will do (Buy for $…, Finance it, Lease it, Claim your free car) instead of always "Start test drive". If you're short on cash for buying outright, it tells you how much more you need.
  • Standard license plates no longer lose their last digit.

Version 156 · Big conveyor car wash, Dodge Charger and Hornet

🫧 Strata Car Wash

  • The small washes by the gas stations are gone. In their place: one big commercial conveyor car wash on the west side, near the Grand River shops (it's in the navigation list).
  • Three pay lanes with kiosks and gates: stop by a kiosk to pay $12 and the gate lifts. Follow the U-turn lane round to the 27 m tunnel, line up and shift to Neutral. The conveyor pulls you through the soap, the spinning brushes, the rinse and the dryers. Teslas and Rivians turn on Car Wash Mode by themselves.
  • 16 vacuum bays under the canopy and an office building. Drive through a gate without paying and you pay for the gate arm too.

Dodge

  • 2025 Dodge Charger Sixpack (twin-turbo I6, AWD): R/T (420 hp) and Scat Pack (550 hp), as a 2-door or a 4-door.
  • 2025 Dodge Charger Daytona (electric, AWD): R/T (496 hp with PowerShot, about 308 mi) and Scat Pack (670 hp, 0-60 in 3.3 s), as a 2-door or a 4-door.
  • 2025 Dodge Hornet: GT and GT Plus (268 hp) and the R/T plug-in hybrid (288 hp, 32 miles on electricity).
  • New body for the Dodge Durango.

Version 155 · Photo mode, DMV and driver's license, car wash, auction, traffic cameras, achievements

📷 Photo mode

  • The camera button at the top left (or F8, or Photos on the phone) pauses the world. Orbit around your car or fly a free camera (WASD, Q/E down/up), pinch or scroll to zoom.
  • Background blur with a focus point you tap, filters (Vivid, Film, Noir, Black & white, Golden, Cool, Cinematic, Retro), exposure, colour, vignette, tilt, lens, a widescreen crop, and the time of day.
  • The big white button saves the picture to Photos on your phone. On a computer, the ⬇ button downloads it.

🪪 Halden DMV and your driver's license

  • New DMV on Maple Blvd (it's in the navigation list). Take the driving test in the car you came in for $25: stop at the stop sign, do a three-point turn in the coned lane, parallel park, then a short drive on the street and back. 15 mph in the lot, 80 points to pass.
  • You now need a driver's license to buy, finance or lease a car (the free first car still works without one). Test drives don't need one.
  • Custom license plates for $150 at the DMV: up to 7 letters and numbers on the back and front of your car. Other players see it online. Every car also has a standard plate now.

🫧 Car wash and dirt

  • Cars get dirty as you drive: slowly on the road, fast off-road and in rain or snow. You can see it on the paint.
  • Strata Car Wash by the gas stations ($12): drive in, shift to Neutral and the conveyor pulls you through soap, brushes, rinse and dryers. Teslas and Rivians turn on Car Wash Mode by themselves.

🔨 Halden Auto Auction

  • New Auction app on the phone. Every 7th game day, from 8 AM to 8 PM, six cars go under the hammer: used cars, wrecks with salvage titles, and one rare car. Preview the lots all week.
  • Bid against other bidders; a late bid adds 10 minutes. Win and the car goes to your garage (cash only). Wrecks keep their damage until a body shop fixes them. Sell it from the Garage for more than you paid.

📸 Speed and red-light cameras

  • Red-light cameras at some traffic lights and speed cameras on some streets (with PHOTO ENFORCED signs). Go more than 10 mph over, or run a red, and they flash.
  • The next morning the ticket arrives in the new Mail app on your phone, with the photo of your car, your speed and your plate. The fine comes out of your account.

🏆 Achievements

  • 25 achievements, like Triple digits (100 mph), High-mileage hero (1,000 miles in one car), Perfect valet, Ghost (escape the police at 3 stars), Collector (10 cars), Millionaire, Licensed and The flip. A gold banner pops up when you unlock one.
  • See them all in the Account panel (person button at the top left). They save with your game and your account.

🐐 Tesla Boombox and Light Show

  • Boombox in the Tesla Toybox: Goat, Applause, La Cucaracha, Rubber Ducky, Sax, Fart and Bike bell from the outside speaker. In Park, the horn plays it.
  • Two new Light Show songs: Holiday Party and Midnight Drive.

Version 154 · Steering wheels with force feedback, Escalade and Expedition screens

Steering wheels

  • Plug in a USB steering wheel and pedals (Logitech, Thrustmaster, Fanatec, Moza and others) and set it up in Settings › Controls › Steering wheel: turn the wheel, press each pedal and pull the paddles once and the game learns them. A clutch pedal works on the manual cars.
  • The car's front wheels follow your wheel exactly through the steering ratio. You can change the rotation (270° to 1080°), the force strength and the steering ratio.
  • Force feedback on Logitech G29, G923 (PlayStation version), G27, G25 and Driving Force GT in Chrome or Edge: press Connect force feedback. The wheel gets heavier with speed, goes light when the front tyres slide, kicks over bumps, potholes and kerbs, jolts in a crash, stops at the car's steering lock, and turns by itself when Super Cruise, Lane Keep or Park Assist steer. Grab it to take over. The rev lights on the wheel light up with the engine speed.
  • Other wheels steer and drive normally, with rumble if the wheel supports it.

Cadillac Escalade

  • The Premium Luxury and Sport Platinum now have the real 55-inch curved screen across the whole dash, like the Escalade-V: the Escalade gauges in front of you, the map in the middle, and the clock, weather and music on the passenger side. The touchscreen is the lower screen on the centre stack again.
  • The Escalade's big screen now has a Cadillac look instead of the Lincoln one.

Ford Expedition

  • The 24-inch panoramic display across the top of the dash: outside temperature and assist lights, your car on its lane with the speed limit and your speed, the gear selector (P R N D M), range and trip, and the map on the right. The Expedition MAX has it too.

Alerts

  • Car alerts and messages show as normal pop-ups on the screen again instead of cards in the gauge cluster. The warning lights stay in the cluster.

Version 153 · New Ford bodies, F-350 & F-450 dually, people walk around cars

Ford

  • New, more detailed bodies for the F-150, Super Duty, Ranger, Maverick, Bronco Sport, Expedition, Mustang Mach-E, Transit and E-Transit.
  • New: the F-350 Super Duty (XLT and Lariat) and the F-450 Super Duty dually with dual rear wheels (Lariat and Platinum).
  • New: the Expedition MAX, the long-wheelbase Expedition (Platinum and King Ranch).
  • The Fusion, the 2007 Mustang, the Escape and the Explorer stay as they were.

Pedestrians

  • People on foot now look where they're going: they walk around parked and stopped cars (including yours) instead of walking into them, step aside on the sidewalk, and wait or turn back when the way is blocked.
  • Someone bumping into your car while it's standing still no longer counts as hitting a pedestrian.

Version 152 · Manual gearbox only on real manual cars

Manual gearbox

  • The manual gearbox with clutch now only works on cars that really come with a stick shift: the Honda Civic Si and Civic Type R, the Acura Integra Type S, and the 2007 Ford Mustang V6, GT, GT Premium and Shelby GT500. Every other car drives as the automatic it really is, even with the setting on, and the setting only shows when you're in one of these cars.

Version 151 · Navigate to places, scroll the list and the map

Navigation

  • Navigate on the car's screen now lists real places instead of roads: Fresh Market, Tread Center, Bean & Brew, HomeWorks, Burger Barn, both Fuel Stops, the service plaza, the Park & charge lot, the Fort St parking garage, the toll plaza, the off-road park, the proving ground, Rosedale, your home and the valet stand. Each shows what it is and how far away it is, nearest first.
  • Drag the list up and down (or use the mouse wheel) to scroll through it.
  • Drag the map to look around, and use the mouse wheel on it to zoom. Tap Recenter to snap back to your car (it also snaps back by itself after 20 seconds).
  • Buttons on the screen now press when you lift your finger, so a drag doesn't press anything by accident.

Version 150 · Admin tools, VR menu and hand tracking

VR on Meta Quest 3

  • VR menu you can see in the headset. Touch the small teal tab to the left of the steering wheel, or hold the right stick click for a second. Change the view, seat height, haptics, graphics, units, manual gearbox and wipers, recenter your seat, or exit VR.
  • Point and click. Aim a controller at the menu and pull the trigger, or just reach out and touch the buttons.
  • Touch the screen. Tap the car's centre screen with a fingertip or the tip of a controller to use it.
  • Hand tracking. Put the controllers down and use your hands: make a fist on the steering wheel rim and turn it, pinch with your right hand for gas and your left hand for brake. You'll see your hands in the car.
  • Car alerts now show in the cluster in VR too.

Announcements and events

  • Messages from the game team and live events now show in a bar at the top of the screen. Events can be double or triple cash from gigs and level-ups, free gas and charging, or a sale on new cars.

Report a player

  • Signed in? Open your account (person icon) to report a player who's causing trouble. An admin will look at it.

Version 149 · Warning lights and cluster alerts

Warning lights

  • The instrument cluster now has real warning lights along the bottom, in the usual colours: red for stop now, amber for check soon, green, blue and white for things that are on. Seatbelt, parking brake, engine too hot, low fuel or low battery, check engine (limp mode), low tire pressure, ABS and traction control working, automatic emergency braking off, open recall, driver alert (take a break), icy outside temperature, off-road mode on, hill descent, adaptive cruise, lane keeping, auto stop/start, low beams and high beams.

Cluster alerts

  • Car notifications now pop up in the cluster as a card with a symbol, like a real car: a coffee cup for driver alert, a shock absorber for the suspension, a mountain for terrain modes, a no-entry sign for wrong way, a tire for tire pressure, two cars for collision warnings and so on.
  • All of the car's notifications go to the cluster while you're in the driver's seat, not just the new systems. Things that aren't the car (money, gigs, your phone, your account) still show as normal messages.

Version 148 · Save your game reminder

Accounts

  • If you're not signed in, after about 3 minutes of driving the game suggests making a free account so your cars and cash are saved. Tap Not now and it asks again later (at most three times per visit).

Version 147 · Alerts in the cluster, self-cancelling signals, wrecked roads

Car alerts

  • Messages from the car itself now pop up in the instrument cluster while you're in the driver's seat (on Tesla, on the screen), like a real car, instead of at the top of the screen. That includes drowsiness and eyes-on-road warnings, air suspension and ride height, drive modes and terrain modes, the sway bar, wrong way, emergency stop, safe exit, cross-traffic, brake fade, engine heat, octane, lockers, recalls, software updates and more. From outside the car they still show as normal messages.

Turn signals

  • The turn signal now cancels itself when you turn the wheel into the turn and let it come back, like a real car. A small nudge for a lane change leaves it on.

My Mode

  • The My Mode settings now only show on the Chevrolet, GMC and Cadillac models that really have My Mode. Other cars keep their own custom mode (Individual, My Drive and so on).

Road condition

  • New Wrecked setting for potholes and bumps, past Destroyed: more than twice as many potholes, craters up to a car-length wide and over 20 cm deep, and roads heaved like after an earthquake.

Version 146 · Round blind-spot view

Blind-spot cameras

  • On Hyundai and Kia, the Blind-Spot View Monitor now opens as a circle inside the gauge on the side you're signalling, growing out from the middle like the real thing: the tachometer for a left signal, the speedometer for a right one. It has the orange guide line along the side of the car.

Version 145 · Head-up display on the glass

Head-up display

  • The head-up display is now projected onto the windshield right above the dashboard, like in the real car. It stays put on the glass when you look around or change your seat height, instead of floating out past the hood.

Version 144 · Blind-spot cameras, higher seat

Blind-spot cameras

  • On the cars that have it for real, turning on your signal now shows a live camera view down that side of the car. On Hyundai and Kia the gauge on that side turns into the camera (Blind-Spot View Monitor), on Tesla the repeater camera pops up on the screen, and on Rivian it shows in the driver display.
  • Cars with it: Kia EV9 Land, GT-Line and GT · Telluride X-Pro SX-Prestige and SX-Prestige · Sorento X-Line SX-Prestige and PHEV · Sportage SX-Prestige Hybrid and X-Line Prestige PHEV · Niro Hybrid SX · Carnival SX-Prestige · EV6 GT-Line and GT · K5 EX and GT · K4 with the Technology Package · Hyundai Palisade Limited and Calligraphy (2022 and 2026) · Santa Fe Limited and Calligraphy · Tucson Limited · Santa Cruz Limited · Kona and Kona Electric Limited · IONIQ 5 Limited · IONIQ 9 Calligraphy · every Tesla · every Rivian.
  • You can turn it off in the driver assist settings.

Seat

  • Everyone now starts in the Higher seat position, so you can see over the dashboard in every car. You can still change it in Settings › Seat.

Version 143 · Quest 3 controls and haptics

VR on Meta Quest 3

  • Every button on the Touch controllers now does something:
    Right: trigger = gas · A = Drive / Reverse · B = Park when stopped, parking brake when moving · grip tap = change view, hold grip = recenter your seat · stick left / right = turn signals · stick up = high beams · stick down = wipers · stick click = adaptive cruise on / off.
    Left: trigger = brake · stick = steer (up / down sets the cruise speed while cruise is on) · X = horn · Y = headlights, hold Y = hazards · grip = parking brake · stick click = start / stop the engine.
  • With the manual gearbox on: left grip is the clutch, A shifts up and B shifts down.
  • Haptics: the controllers now rumble with the car. You feel the engine hum grow with the revs, a click on every gear change, bumps, potholes, kerbs and rumble strips, gravel and dirt, ABS pulsing in your brake hand, wheelspin in your gas hand, the lane departure warning in your steering hand, the rev limiter, and a big jolt in a crash. Every button press gives a small tap. The Haptics setting turns it off.

Version 142 · Player roles

Accounts

  • Players can now have a role, like Contributor, shown next to their name on their account.
  • Gifts from the game team (money, or loans paid off) now land in your game within a minute, even if you're playing right then, and save to your account straight away.

Version 141 · Instant saves

Accounts

  • Your game now saves to your account within a few seconds of buying, selling, leasing or financing a car, getting paid or spending money, on top of the save every minute.

Version 140 · Shift is the clutch

Manual gearbox

  • With the manual gearbox on (Settings › Controls), the clutch is now Shift instead of Ctrl. Hold Shift, then Q to shift up or E to shift down.
  • While the manual gearbox is on, tapping Shift no longer sets the parking brake (use P), and Shift no longer makes the throttle and brakes gentle.

Version 139 · Account sign-in fix

Accounts

  • Fixed the game reloading over and over after you signed in on a second device (like your phone).
  • When your account's game loads on a device, that device's own game is now kept as a backup. If the wrong one loaded, open your account (person icon, top left) and tap Use that one instead.
  • Your progress is kept through game updates while you're signed in.

Version 138 · Accounts, new Kias, terrain modes

Accounts

  • Make an account with just a username and a password: no email. Tap the person icon at the top left, or Account on the start screen.
  • Your cars, cash, bank, phone, gigs and houses save to your account every minute and when you close the page. Sign in on another device and your game is there.
  • Your progress also comes back after a game update, instead of starting over.
  • There's no password reset, so pick one you'll remember.

Kia lineup

  • New: the 2026 Kia K5 in LXS, GT-Line, GT-Line AWD, EX and the 290 hp GT.
  • New: the K4 sedan in LX, LXS, EX, GT-Line and GT-Line Turbo, next to the K4 hatchback.
  • New bodies and cabins for the K4 hatchback, Seltos, Sportage, Sorento, Telluride, Carnival, Niro, Niro EV, EV6 and EV9.

Terrain modes

  • Every car with real off-road modes now has them on the terrain control too: Jeep Selec-Terrain (Cherokee, Compass, Grand Wagoneer, Recon, Wagoneer S Trailhawk), Hyundai and Kia Terrain Mode, Rivian All-Terrain, Soft Sand and Rock Crawl, and more. The terrain control and the drive mode button change the same setting.
  • The AWD Sorento, Sportage, EV6 and EV9 get Kia's Terrain Mode: Snow, Mud and Sand.
  • Fixed the terrain button doing nothing on cars with a terrain dial, like the Grand Cherokee L.

Test drives

  • You can test drive each car once. To drive it again, buy, finance or lease it (your first car is still free). Used cars on the lots count one by one.

Faster loading

  • Removed the old Strata cars that were no longer in the game, and shrank the stand-in car shown while models load. The game file is about 10% smaller and starts a little faster.

Version 137 · Rocks you can't fly off, lower wipers

Rocks and ledges

  • Hitting boulders no longer throws your car into the air. Before, a tyre jumped straight to the top of a rock the moment it touched it.
  • Now a tyre feels a rock when the front of the tread touches it, then rolls up the face. It can only climb as fast as a real tyre would.
  • Rock faces push back. Hit a boulder too fast and the car slows hard or stops against it instead of launching. A rock taller than your tyre stops you like a wall.
  • When the suspension bottoms out on a big hit, it soaks up the blow instead of bouncing the car back up.
  • Crawling over the rocks, the Steps ledges and the logs works like before, minus the bouncing. Same for the rock lane at the proving ground.

Wipers

  • Parked wipers now sit lower, tucked into the cowl at the bottom of the windshield, so you no longer see them in front of the screen. They still sweep the whole glass when they're on.

Version 136 · Real Kia warning chimes

Kia sounds

  • Every Kia now uses its real recorded chimes: the forward collision warning, the solid tone when automatic emergency braking is braking for you, the blind-spot warning when you signal toward a car beside you, the lane departure warning, the notification chime and the chime when you shift into reverse.

Version 135 · Halden Off-Road Park, Grand Cherokee L, Grand Wagoneer L, 2022 Palisade

Halden Off-Road Park

  • A new off-road park in the hills west of County Rd 12 (pick Off-road park in the start menu, or turn in at the trailhead lot just south of the proving ground). A dirt trail loops through it with a board at every obstacle, rated like a real park: green circle, blue square, black diamond.
  • Boulder Alley (black diamond): a 120 m rock garden. Every rock is its own shape: chipped faces, flat tops, cracks, some leaning, in granite gray, sandstone tan and dark basalt, with big boulders walling the trail in. The rocks you see are exactly what your tyres climb.
  • The Steps (blue square): three rock ledges, 30 to 45 cm high.
  • The Bog (blue square): a sunken mud pit about 60 cm deep with ruts and muddy water at the bottom. Keep your momentum.
  • Log Crossing (green circle): three logs across the trail.
  • Off-Camber (blue square): a section where the trail tilts about 15°.
  • Widowmaker (black diamond): an 8 m hill with a 30% climb.
  • The trees in the park are solid, so stay on the trail. Crawl Control, Trail Control, Selec-Speed, lockers and the terrain modes all work here.

New Jeeps and an older Palisade

  • 2026 Jeep Grand Cherokee L (3 rows): Laredo 4x2 (3.6 V6, 293 hp), Limited and Limited Reserve 4x4 (2.0 Hurricane, 324 hp), Summit 4x4 with Quadra-Lift air suspension.
  • 2026 Jeep Grand Wagoneer L (long-wheelbase): 4x4, Limited and Summit Reserve, 3.0 Hurricane twin-turbo I6 (420 hp), Quadra-Lift air suspension.
  • 2022 Hyundai Palisade (the first generation): SE, SEL, Limited and Calligraphy, 3.8 V6 (291 hp). Limited and Calligraphy have HTRAC AWD and Highway Driving Assist.
  • New, more detailed bodies for the Jeep Compass, Cherokee, Grand Cherokee, Grand Wagoneer, Wagoneer S and Recon.

Version 134 · New left-side dock

Left-side buttons

  • The key, phone and Bluetooth buttons are now one glass dock, and each shows its state underneath: Locked (green) or Unlocked (amber) with a padlock that opens and closes, Linked (blue) when your phone is connected, and a red badge on the phone for unread messages.
  • The Screen button moved into the dock. It only shows in the driver's seat view and switches to Road while you're looking at the screen.
  • The little arrow under the dock shrinks it to icons only; it remembers your choice.

Version 133 · Valet parking job

Halden Valet

  • New gig in the phone's Gig Jobs app: 🔑 Valet. Start a shift, park your own car near the Cass Ave garage and walk to the valet stand on the sidewalk.
  • Guests pull up at the curb in nice cars (BMW, Escalade, Lucid, Rivian, Mercedes and more). Walk up, take the keys, drive it into the garage and park it in any free stall on any level, nose in between the lines. Shift to P and get out.
  • When a guest is ready to leave you get their ticket number and level. Tap Run there to jog to the car, then bring it down to the stand. The guest drives away in it.
  • Pay is $7 a car plus a tip for speed: up to $14 for parking and $25 for a quick return. Any new dent or scratch costs you the tip and comes out of your pay. Keep it under 15 mph in the garage.
  • The garage gates open for you on the job, and a yellow marker shows the car or the stand. Your own car waits where you left it, with its fuel and damage just as they were.

Version 132 · Escalade lower screen, tire air machines, Hwy 7 toll plaza

Cadillac Escalade

  • The main touchscreen now lives in the lower screen under the 55-inch display, where the real 2026 Escalade has it. The big curved screen shows the gauges, the map and the clock, weather and media across the dash.

Tire air at gas stations

  • Every gas station now has a red air machine near the pumps. Park close, walk up and tap Air for your tires · $2.00: all four tires go back to 35 psi. A slow leak keeps leaking until it's patched (phone › car app, or Tread Center).

Toll plaza on Hwy 7

  • A toll plaza with booths in every lane, a canopy and lane lights, in both directions. The toll is $2.50 ($5.00 with a trailer).
  • Right lane, CASH: stop at the booth, pay, and the gate arm lifts. Drive through it and you break the gate and get a $50 violation by mail.
  • Other lanes, E-ZPass: with a tag ($10 in Settings › Assists › Your car) the toll comes off as you pass. Without one, a toll-by-plate bill with a $5 fee arrives in the mail.
  • Traffic slows down for the plaza, stays in its lane, and cars in the cash lane stop at the booth.

Version 131 · Engine heat, hot brakes, fuel grades, dashcam replays, off-road tools and more

Where to find them

  • Settings › Assists, under the safety systems: Off-road, your car's air suspension, More car features and a Your car summary (outside temperature, engine temperature, fuel, alignment, alarm, dashcam, insurance, updates and recalls).

Driving

  • Outside temperature now follows the season and time of day (cold January mornings, hot July afternoons, the odd heat wave), and the screens show it.
  • Engine heat: slow traffic on a hot day, towing something heavy or a cracked radiator push the temperature up. Around 234°F the A/C switches itself off; above 243°F you lose power until it cools. The gauge on the cluster moves.
  • Hot brakes: ride the brakes down a long hill and you get a hot-brake smell warning, then brake fade (a soft pedal) and smoke from the wheels.
  • Alignment: a hard pothole hit can knock it out. The car pulls to one side and wears its tires faster until Tread Center fixes it ($129).
  • Rev-matching on manual downshifts for the cars that have it (Civic Type R, Integra Type S). In other cars, blip the throttle with the clutch in or the car lurches.

Fuel

  • Pick a grade at the pump: Regular 87, Midgrade 89 or Premium 93. Cars that need premium lose about 6% power on regular; turbo engines that only recommend it lose a little.
  • Fuel door and charge port on the correct side for the cars we know. The arrow next to the fuel (or battery) icon shows which side; park with the pump on that side or the hose won't reach.

Security and cameras

  • While you're away from your parked car, someone may try the door. Locked cars set off the alarm and your brand's app sends an alert (myChevrolet, FordPass, Toyota app, and so on). Unlocked cars get robbed.
  • Tesla Sentry Mode and Rivian Gear Guard flash the lights and save a clip. Dog Mode (Tesla) and Pet Comfort (Rivian) show the "My owner will be back soon" screen.
  • Locked doors now stop the person who walks up to your car at a red light.
  • Dashcam replays: on cars with a dashcam (Tesla, Rivian, newer Hyundai/Kia/Genesis Built-in Cam, BMW Drive Recorder, Mercedes, or the dealer add-on), crashes and near misses save the last 30 seconds. Watch them back with slow-mo; F8 replays the last 30 seconds any time.

Owning the car

  • Insurance: tickets raise your premium for 3 years. At the body shop you can file a claim: insurance pays, you pay the $500 deductible, and the premium goes up for 3 years.
  • Software updates over the air on the brands that really send them (Tesla, Rivian, Lucid, Ford Power-Up, GM, BMW, Mercedes, Hyundai/Kia/Genesis, Volvo, VW, Audi, Toyota and Lexus). BlueCruise and Super Cruise cars without lane changes get them in an update. You install from Settings while parked.
  • Recalls: now and then a recall notice arrives for your model, and you may notice the problem (a rear camera that blacks out, an engine that runs hot or stalls, charging capped at 80%). Dealer service at Tread Center fixes it for free, along with an inspection, any update, alignment and oil. It's free in the first 2 years on Toyota and Lexus and 3 years on BMW.

Off-road and suspension

  • Low-speed off-road cruise under each brand's name: Toyota CRAWL Control, Lexus Crawl Control, Ford Trail Control, Jeep Selec-Speed Control.
  • Ford Trail 1-Pedal Drive and GM Terrain mode: lift off and the truck brakes for you. Ford Trail Turn Assist turns about 20% tighter.
  • Lockers on pavement now scrub and fight the turn, like real ones.
  • Air suspension heights on Ram (Active-Level), Jeep (Quadra-Lift), Chevy/GMC/Cadillac (Air Ride) and Rivian: Entry/Exit (lowers when you park and get out), Aero (drops above 55 mph), Normal and off-road heights with their real speed limits.
